body: European Sleep Research Society (ESRS)
guidelineTitle: European guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of insomnia
status: superseded by ESRS European Insomnia Guideline 2023
recommendation: 2017 abstract: CBT-I 'recommended as the first-line treatment for chronic insomnia in adults of any age (strong recommendation, high-quality evidence)'. Drugs 'can be offered if CBT-I is not sufficiently effective or not available'. 'Benzodiazepines, benzodiazepine receptor agonists and some antidepressants are effective in the short-term treatment of insomnia (≤4 weeks; weak recommendation, moderate-quality evidence)'. 'Antihistamines, antipsychotics, melatonin and phytotherapeutics are not recommended (strong to weak recommendations, low- to very-low-quality evidence)'. Light therapy and exercise 'need to be further evaluated' (weak, low quality). Homeopathy, acupuncture not recommended (weak, very low).

citation.authors: Riemann D, Baglioni C, Bassetti C, et al.
citation.title: European guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of insomnia

notes: What changed in 2023: grading moved from GRADE strong/weak to A-D; orexin antagonists added (up to 3 months, A); PR melatonin >55 y gained a role (B) while 2017 rejected melatonin outright; light/exercise moved from 'needs evaluation' to adjunct (B); digital CBT-I named as equal delivery route (A); 2017 drugs were 'not available' fallback, 2023 drops 'or not available'. 2017 was based on the German S3 guideline and endorsed by the World Sleep Society.

body: European Commission
guidelineTitle: Commission Directive 2014/85/EU (driving licences, Annex III section 11: obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome)
recommendation: 11.2: moderate OSAS = AHI 15-29, severe = AHI ≥30, 'both associated with excessive daytime sleepiness'. 11.3: suspected moderate/severe OSAS 'shall be referred for further authorised medical advice before a driving licence is issued or renewed. They may be advised not to drive until confirmation of the diagnosis.' 11.4: licences may be issued if 'adequate control of their condition and compliance with appropriate treatment and improvement of sleepiness'. 11.5: periodic review 'at intervals not exceeding three years for drivers of group 1 and one year for drivers of group 2'.

body: Helsedirektoratet (Norwegian Directorate of Health)
guidelineTitle: Nasjonal veileder for vanedannende legemidler
status: current (first published 19 Oct 2021, last change 30 Apr 2025); replacement 'avhengighetsskapende legemidler' in consultation draft (March 2026)
recommendation: 'Behandlingsvarigheten med benzodiazepiner eller benzodiazepinlignende legemidler bør være så kort som mulig, maksimalt fire uker.' Indication: 'Søvnlidelser, vanligvis inntil to uker, maksimalt fire uker.' Intermittent use: benzodiazepines daily or every other day up to 14 days before a drug-free pause; Z-drugs every other evening. Up to 2 weeks can stop without taper; after 2-4 weeks taper gradually. Prescribe no more than the smallest pack.
